## What the data says
- No PSI microgravity test runs exist for thin fabric at 34% O₂, 56.5 kPa (target conditions) → **not covered by PSI data** [PSI-25] [PSI-99]
- The predictor gives a physics estimate of flame temperature ≈ 2610 K, which is ~290 K above the hottest thin-fabric run (≈ 2320 K) and ~600 K above the coldest burning thin-fabric run (≈ 2010 K) [PSI-25] [PSI-99]
- All solid-material runs (including thin fabrics) were performed at 13.6-22.2 % O₂ and ~101 kPa in microgravity; 131 of 134 runs sustained burning, leaving only 3 non-burning runs, so a flammability limit cannot be located [PSI-25] [PSI-98][PSI-99]
- Fire-resistant materials (silicone, Nomex) did not burn at ≤ 22.2 % O₂: 0/4 silicone runs burned, 3/4 Nomex runs burned [PSI-25] [PSI-99]
- Outside PSI, Nomex HT90-40 failed NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 at 30 % O₂, 70.1 kPa in 1 g (NASA report) (NTRS 20070018178)
- Partial-gravity data are absent; NASA FM2 researchers note that flame-spread oxygen requirements may be lowest near lunar gravity, making partial gravity potentially more hazardous (NTRS 20260000646)

## How confident we can be
- Evidence coverage for thin fabric at the target oxygen level and pressure is zero; confidence is limited to the physics estimate only.
- Solid-material data are dominated by sustained burns (131/134), so the dataset cannot define a flammability limit for any solid, including thin fabrics.
- Fire-resistant material data are limited to 8 runs at ≤ 22.2 % O₂; no runs exist at the target 34 % O₂, reducing confidence for those materials.

## Gaps
- No microgravity thin-fabric tests at 34 % O₂ or at 56.5 kPa (target pressure).
- No partial-gravity (lunar or Martian) combustion tests for any material class.
- No high-oxygen (≥ 30 % O₂) fire-resistant material tests; material-specific limits remain unknown.
- Lack of non-burning solid runs prevents locating a flammability limit for thin fabrics.

## What future experiments (e.g. LUCI, FM2) should measure
- Thin-fabric ignition and flame spread at 34 % O₂ and 56.5 kPa in microgravity to provide direct evidence coverage.
- Partial-gravity (0.16 g, 0.38 g) thin-fabric tests to assess whether reduced gravity increases hazard relative to micro- and 1-g.
- Fire-resistant material (silicone, Nomex) burns at ≥ 30 % O₂ and varied pressures to define material-specific oxygen limits.
- Additional solid runs that intentionally extinguish (e.g., higher flow speeds, lower O₂) to create non-burning data points for locating flammability limits.
- Validation of the physics estimate by comparing predicted flame temperatures with measured temperatures for thin fabrics under the target conditions.
